title: microStudio games reference
summary: The microStudio commands and Python from Games with microStudio, each with what it does. Copy a card into your game.

items.label: def init
items.hint: Runs once, when the game starts. Give your variables their first values here. The engine calls it: you never do.

items.label: def update
items.hint: Runs 60 times a second. Move things, check keys and keep score here. A variable it changes needs a global line.

items.label: def draw
items.hint: Runs after each update. Clear the screen, then draw everything where it is now. Change nothing here.
items.example:
x = -80

def update():
    global x
    x += 1

def draw():
    screen.clear("rgb(10,10,40)")
    screen.fillRound(x, 0, 16, 16, "rgb(255,210,0)")
items.shows: Draws the dot where x is now; update moves it a little each frame.

items.label: global
items.hint: The first line inside a function that changes a variable made outside it. Without it, Python stops with "cannot access local variable".

items.label: screen.clear
items.hint: Fills the whole screen with one colour. Put it first in draw(), or the last frame stays on the screen.

items.label: screen.fillRect
items.hint: A filled box. x and y are its middle: (0, 0) is the middle of the screen, y goes up to 100 at the top.

items.label: screen.fillRound
items.hint: A filled circle or oval, centred on x and y. Same width and height for a circle.

items.label: screen.drawRect and drawRound
items.hint: Outlines only: the same as fillRect and fillRound, without filling the inside.

items.label: screen.drawLine
items.hint: A straight line from one point to another.

items.label: screen.drawText
items.hint: Writes text centred on x and y. A number must be joined as text: "Score: " + str(score).
items.example:
score = 3

def draw():
    screen.clear("rgb(10,10,40)")
    screen.drawText("Score: " + str(score), 0, 80, 12, "white")
    screen.drawText("GAME OVER", 0, 0, 24, "rgb(255,120,120)")

items.label: Colours
items.hint: A colour is text: a name, rgb(red, green, blue) with numbers from 0 to 255, or a hex code.
items.example:
def draw():
    screen.clear("rgb(10,10,40)")
    screen.fillRound(-60, 0, 40, 40, "red")
    screen.fillRound(0, 0, 40, 40, "rgb(255,210,0)")
    screen.fillRound(60, 0, 40, 40, "#40a0ff")

items.label: screen.drawSprite
items.hint: Draws a picture you made in microStudio's Sprites tab, by its name. Sprites need microstudio.dev: in our playground nothing appears.

items.label: pressed
items.code:
def pressed(key):
    return hasattr(keyboard, key) and keyboard[key] != 0
items.hint: Copy this helper into your game once. pressed("LEFT") is True while the key is held. Key names: LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN, SPACE, A to Z.

items.label: Move with keys
items.hint: Inside update(): a held key moves the player a little every frame, so it glides.

items.label: Stay on the screen
items.hint: After moving, put the player back if it has gone past an edge. The top is y = 100 and the bottom is y = -100.

items.label: mouse
items.hint: Where the mouse is, in the same coordinates as drawing. mouse.pressed is 1 while the button is held, else 0.

items.label: audio.beep
items.hint: Plays notes from text. Put it where something happens in update(), once, not in draw(). Try "duration 100 C E G" or "saw C2".

items.label: class with move and draw
items.hint: Each object keeps its own x and y in self, moves itself and draws itself.
items.shows: Four Star objects, each drawn at its own x.

items.label: A list of objects
items.hint: In update(), tell every object to move; in draw(), tell every object to draw. The loop stays short however many there are.

items.label: random.randint
items.hint: A whole number picked at random from the first to the second, both included. import random goes at the top of the game.

items.label: touches
items.code:
def touches(self, x, y):
    return abs(self.x - x) < ‹12› and abs(self.y - y) < ‹8›
items.hint: True when this object is close to (x, y) in both directions: abs() is the distance, whichever side it is on.

items.label: print
items.hint: Writes in the console under the game: useful to check a value while the game runs.
